spec_match.rationale: Contrasts the @counter-style rule with the anonymous symbols() form and demonstrates the real namespace-collision failure with two same-named @counter-style rules whose later declaration wins in the cascade.

interactive.rationale: The component-count slider live-regenerates both CSS listings, the cost table and the tally; verified moving it from 3 to 7 updated all readouts (69 lines/7 names vs 27 lines/0).

blurb_alignment.rationale: The card promises the argument for the shape via name/colocation/collision costs, and the page delivers each with live evidence.

edge_cases.rationale: The clash section is a genuine failure-mode demo, but the page has no unsupported-browser handling at all: on a pre-154 browser the example lists silently render decimal markers with no explanation.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5146996093616128 and the @counter-style rule in CSS Counter Styles 3.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite proves the parse and render contracts this page relies on; on Chromium 141 the route honestly reported 1 pass / 7 fail since symbols() needs Chrome 154.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): slider exercised, clash verified (clash-a resolved to the redefined 'markers' style and rendered the wrong ✗ bullets as intended), console clean, no failed same-origin requests, desktop and mobile screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Loads demo-telemetry.js and emits a comparison-rendered assert with counts and support state.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, rose/emerald panel accents, captioned cost table, no static card — though a few inline style attributes on the clash headings could move into the stylesheet.

accessibility.rationale: The slider has a real label with a live value span, both outputs are aria-live, code listings are focusable, and the cost table has caption plus scoped headers.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 (scrollWidth 360, screenshot read); panels stack via auto-fit and code blocks scroll internally.

openQuestions.title: Add the sibling pages' support banner and label the fallback lists
openQuestions.detail: Unlike counters-in-content and system-explorer, this page computes SUPPORTED but never surfaces it. On Chromium 141 the two 'same result' example lists render plain decimal under headings that claim symbols() output, and the emerald clash panel captioned 'Nothing to collide with: the style has no name' also shows decimal — the visual contradicts the caption with no explanation. Reuse the .support banner pattern and, when unsupported, annotate the example lists ('markers shown are this browser's fallback; on Chrome 154 both lists show ◆ ◇') so the page never looks like a broken comparison.

summary: Reviewed at http://localhost:3000/v154/css-symbols/inline-vs-named/ with Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp), which genuinely lacks symbols() (pre-Chrome-154). The comparison machinery, slider, cost table and the @counter-style namespace-clash demo all work — the clash is fully demonstrable on this build and correctly showed component A receiving the redefining component's ✗ markers. The real gap is capability honesty: this is the one page in the feature without a support banner, so its symbols()-marked example lists silently degrade to decimal while the surrounding copy claims otherwise. Desktop 1280 and mobile 360 DPR3 screenshots read, no overflow, console/network clean bar the sandbox font-CDN artifact; /conformance/ honestly reported 1 pass / 7 fail on this build.
